metadata.title: Matematik og natur/teknologi i 4. klasse: Resultater af TIMSS-undersøgelsen 2023

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study reports Danish results from TIMSS 2023 for 4th-grade students in mathematics and science/technology. The analytic sample is based on the TIMSS sampling design (random two-stage cluster sampling of schools and intact classes) with exclusions applied according to international quality standards (e.g., excluding schools without 4th grade instruction, special schools, non-Danish instruction, and very small schools; plus post-sampling exclusions for students unable to complete the test). The authors state that TIMSS provides design weights for the student unit and that all analyses in the book are performed using these design weights to represent the population of Danish 4th graders in the relevant domains. They also use plausible values for achievement scaling and analyze with the R package EdSurvey (which supports weighted analyses with PVs). Replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are not described in the provided text, so replicate-weight usage is not reported.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The manuscript describes the use of plausible values (five PVs per student) for TIMSS achievement scaling, but it does not explicitly document how missing data in questionnaire items or other covariates were handled (e.g., whether missing questionnaire responses were imputed, excluded, or handled via a specific method). Given that TIMSS uses complex sampling and PVs, missingness handling for non-achievement variables is a methodological transparency requirement; the absence of a stated strategy represents a reporting gap for the covariate data used in regression/association analyses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The target population is all students enrolled in 4th grade in Denmark in the school year of TIMSS 2023. The sampling frame is based on a cleaned list of Danish schools from the STIL institutions register; the authors initially excluded (i) treatment/assistance provision schools, (ii) schools without 4th-grade instruction, (iii) schools that do not teach in Danish, (iv) special schools, and (v) very small schools with fewer than five 4th-grade students—removing 2.3% from the sampling frame. From the remaining frame, IEA/RTI International drew 164 sampled schools plus replacement schools; 158 Danish schools participated (126 first-sampled + 32 replacement). Within participating schools, intact 4th-grade classes were sampled and (as described) all students in selected classes were eligible, with further exclusions at student level limited to international quality standards (total exclusion 5.2%), and follow-up sessions were used for absent students where possible. The book reports that 5,166 students completed the TIMSS study in Denmark, and analyses are conducted with TIMSS design weights.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Weighted mean score: 523.7 (SE 2.1) in 2023 vs 524.5 (SE 1.9) in 2019 (difference -0.8, p=0.77). Gender gap in 2023: 15.4 points (SE 2.6), p<0.001. Socioeconomic status explains ~12% of variance in mathematics (R2=0.12).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2023 Grade 4 Mathematics the study leveraged gender, socioeconomic status, and student/context measures (e.g., motivation, self-efficacy, instructional clarity) to describe mathematics achievement, finding that the overall mean was stable from 2019 to 2023 while the gender gap widened substantially in boys’ favor and socioeconomic status remained a significant predictor of achievement (R2≈0.12). The book reports weighted PV-based TIMSS scaling but does not present ML model training; therefore, no predictive ML performance metrics are applicable. main_findings.performance_metrics: Weighted mean score: 522.1 (SE 2.6) in 2023 vs 522.2 (SE 2.4) in 2019 (difference -0.0, p=0.99). Gender difference in 2023: 1.3 points (SE 2.6), p=0.63 (not significant). Socioeconomic status explains ~17% of variance in science/technology (R2=0.17).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2023 Grade 4 Science/Technology the study leveraged gender, socioeconomic status, and student/context measures (e.g., motivation, self-efficacy, disruptive behavior) to describe science/technology achievement, finding that the overall mean was stable from 2019 to 2023, gender differences were not statistically significant in 2023, and socioeconomic status showed stronger explanatory power than in mathematics (R2≈0.17). The analysis is PV-based and weighted, but it is not an ML predictive modeling study; thus, no ML algorithm comparison is reported. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.outcome_summary: This book reports Danish TIMSS 2023 results for 4th graders in mathematics and science/technology using TIMSS’s PV-based achievement scaling and design weights. For mathematics, the weighted mean score was 523.7 in 2023 versus 524.5 in 2019 (difference -0.8, p=0.77), indicating overall stability, but the gender gap widened markedly: boys scored 15.4 points higher than girls in 2023 (p<0.001). Socioeconomic status explained about 12% of the variance in mathematics achievement (R2=0.12). For science/technology, the weighted mean was 522.1 in 2023 versus 522.2 in 2019 (p=0.99), with no significant gender gap in 2023, while socioeconomic status explained about 17% of variance (R2=0.17). The manuscript emphasizes weighted PV analyses (via EdSurvey) but does not describe any machine-learning model training or missing-data handling strategy for covariates, limiting interpretability for ML-focused purposes.
